heading: Right to discuss terms of contract

children.heading: Producer
children.text: The term “producer” means any person engaged in the raising and caring for livestock or poultry for slaughter.

children.heading: Processor
children.text: The term “processor” means any person engaged in the business of obtaining livestock or poultry for the purpose of slaughtering the livestock or poultry.

tree.heading: No prohibition of discussion
tree.text: Notwithstanding a provision in any contract between a producer and a processor for the production of livestock or poultry, or in any marketing agreement between a producer and a processor for the sale of livestock or poultry for a term of 1 year or more, that provides that information contained in the contract is confidential, a party to the contract shall not be prohibited from discussing any terms or details of the contract with—

children.text: a legal adviser to the party;
an accountant hired by the party;
an executive or manager of the party;
a landlord of the party; or
a member of the immediate family of the party.

preempt any State law that addresses confidentiality provisions in contracts for the sale or production of livestock or poultry, except any provision of State law that makes lawful a contract provision that prohibits a party from, or limits a party in, engaging in discussion that subsection (b) requires to be permitted; or
deprive any State court of jurisdiction under any such State law.

tree.heading: Applicability
tree.text: This section applies to each contract described in subsection (b) that is entered into, amended, renewed, or extended after May 13, 2002.

notes.text: Codification Section was enacted as part of the Farm Security and Rural Investment Act of 2002, and not as part of the Packers and Stockyards Act, 1921, which comprises this chapter.
